page: PDF p. 149 (printed p. 125); related PDF p. 89 (printed 65), Ch. 4
evidence: Rendered image of PDF p. 149 shows the in-figure axis label on the vertical SLO line: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The figure's own caption on the same page reads: "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget — a superset of TTFT violations". Ch. 4, Table 4-1 Latency row (PDF p. 89) defines: "TTFT budget 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); TPOT budget ~25 ms/token; p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s, p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms".
issue: The figure's own axis label calls the 2 s value the "TTFT budget", which is the opposite of the book's definition and of the caption printed directly beneath it: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling. The book treats this pair as load-bearing ("Where a distinction is load-bearing ... the book holds it sharply: synonyms are a readability concession, and load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed", Preface, PDF p. 22). A reader who copies the axis label into a dashboard, an SLO slide or an ADR will record the wrong budget; only the caption corrects it, and a caption is read less often than an axis label.
fix_instruction: Re-render Fig. 6.2 with the in-figure label changed to "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)" (and, if the design budget is also plotted, label it "1.2 s TTFT design budget"). Grep the whole figure set for the string "TTFT budget" applied to the 2 s line and apply the same fix anywhere it appears (any figure reusing the 2 s line).

page: PDF p. 38 (printed 14) and PDF p. 60 (printed 36); convention stated at PDF p. 20 (printed xvi)
evidence: PDF p. 38 (Ch. 1, §1.5, Common Mistakes): "code, numerics, and non-Latin scripts can run 2–5× the naive word-count estimate (rule of thumb; the multiplier is tokenizer- and language-specific) [ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark][HYPOTHESIS]". PDF p. 60 (Ch. 2, §2.5): "actual sustained bandwidth for weight-read kernels may be 60–80% of peak [ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark][HYPOTHESIS][UNMEASURED]". The Preface's label rules (PDF p. 20) state: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; the two tags are set with no space between them and never break across a line", and the Axis-1 vocabulary is the closed set "[1P] / [canonical scenario] / [ILLUSTRATIVE] / [2°] / [LAB]".
issue: Two occurrences embed free prose inside the provenance tag ("[ILLUSTRATIVE: industry rule of thumb, no named survey or benchmark]"), which is not a member of the book's own closed Axis-1 vocabulary and breaks the mandatory one-tag-per-axis, no-space, no-inline-text pair format. The qualifier belongs in the surrounding prose, not inside the brackets. The defect is not cosmetic for this book: the Preface's whole verification scheme depends on labels being machine-parseable tokens, and the second occurrence also stacks a third bracket ([UNMEASURED]) onto a pair, which the Preface permits only as a third axis 'riding along' rather than appended as free text.
fix_instruction: Replace both with the bare tag pair and move the qualifier into the prose immediately before it — e.g. "an industry rule of thumb, with no named survey or benchmark [ILLUSTRATIVE][HYPOTHESIS]" — and re-check the whole document for any other occurrence of a bracketed tag containing a colon or free text (search for "[ILLUSTRATIVE:" and "[1P:").

page: PDF p. 27 (printed 3) and PDF p. 78 (printed 68); convention stated at PDF p. 23 (printed xix)
chapter: Ch. 1 §1.1.2, Ch. 4 (Canonical Workload box) — Appendix A cross-references
evidence: PDF p. 27 (Ch. 1, §1.1.2): "the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next card states a native 262K-token window with YaRN extension to 1M, and the GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4 cards state 1M [1P][FACT] model cards: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next; HF zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash; DeepSeek-V4 technical report, arXiv 2606.19348, and model card HF deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro — all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10". PDF p. 78 (Ch. 4, Canonical Workload box): "Appendix A's §A.7 (Fig A.2, vendor-relative KV/compute ratios) is its deliberate relaxation, not a correction". The Preface's cross-reference convention (PDF p. 23) states: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N."
issue: Both Appendix A references violate the book's own stated appendix-numbering convention: "§10" carries no letter suffix (the convention's example is "9A"), and "§A.7" uses a letter prefix, which is the figure-numbering form (A.N) rather than the section form (N-letter). "§A.7" additionally points at "Fig A.2", so a reader following the section pointer lands on a differently numbered figure, and neither form matches the "9A" pattern used elsewhere in the book ("Appendix A §9A", cited on PDF pp. 46, 66, 79). At least one of the two forms cannot resolve to the appendix's actual section labels.
fix_instruction: Check the actual section labels in Appendix A and rewrite both pointers in the sanctioned form — e.g. "Appendix A §10A" and "Appendix A §7A" — and add "§ 10A" / "§ 7A" style consistency to the appendix's own Contents listing so the labels are discoverable. Sweep the full document for the patterns "Appendix A §", "Appendix A's §" and any bare "§A." to catch the remaining instances.

page: PDF p. 41 (printed 17) vs PDF p. 32 (printed 8); convention noted at PDF p. 22 (printed xviii)
evidence: PDF p. 41 (Ch. 2, §2.1): "The full prefill also has a substantial linear-in-L component — the weight-matmul FLOPs, 2NL (where N = model parameters and L = tokens processed)" — and the same chapter uses L for sequence length again on PDF p. 41: "the attention work grows with the square of the context length" and PDF p. 32 (Ch. 1): "4·n_layers·L·d FLOPs ... 4·n_layers·L·d bytes". Against this, PDF p. 32 (Ch. 1, KV cache section) states: "(The symbol is Mweights, not W: throughout the book W is reserved for mean time in system in Little's law, L = λW, Ch 4.)" — i.e. L is also the Little's-law population of requests in system, as it is in Ch. 2's own use of "L = λW" and in Ch. 4's "Lexec = λ × Wexec".
issue: L carries two unrelated meanings across the same chapters: sequence length (tokens processed) in the FLOP/byte formulas — 2NL, 4·n_layers·L·d, 4·n_layers·L²·d — and the number of requests resident in the system in Little's law (L = λW). The book anticipated one half of this collision (it reserves W against Mweights) but left L doubly bound, and the collision lands inside one chapter: a reader following Ch. 2's "2NL" and then the same chapter's "L = λW" has to re-derive which L applies. Ch. 4 already avoids it by renaming the population L_exec, so the fix is available in the book's own vocabulary.
fix_instruction: Adopt the Ch. 4 convention book-wide: use L_exec (or N_in_system) for the Little's-law population in every occurrence — the Ch. 2 note on PDF p. 32 and the causal-chain/Little's-law passages in Ch. 2 and Ch. 4 — and state both bindings in the Preface's reading conventions next to the existing "Mweights, not W" note, so that 2NL and L = λW can never be confused.
